# CNC Workbench — Controller-grammar rule codes reference

Every controller-grammar lint (`packages/core/src/lints/controllerGrammar.ts`) attaches a stable `code` to each issue.
These codes are mapped to canonical fixes in `packages/core/src/lints/controllerGrammarFixes.ts` (`CG_DUPLICATE_ADDRESSES_*` is a per-letter family).
Downstream tools (IDE quick-fixes, batch auto-fixers, CLI envelope cross-tables) look up fixes by code rather than scraping rule messages.

Total catalogue entries: 6
Live emitted codes verified at generation time: 7 (CG_DUPLICATE_ADDRESSES_X, CG_DUPLICATE_ADDRESSES_Y, CG_DUPLICATE_O_HEADER, CG_FANUC_INVALID_N_O_FORMAT, CG_FANUC_MACRO_IJK_ORDER, CG_FANUC_PROGRAM_ENVELOPE, CG_N_AND_O_MIXED)

| Code | Canonical fix | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CG_DUPLICATE_ADDRESSES_*` | Split duplicate <LETTER> words into two blocks; controller is last-value-wins | Duplicated address letters in one block are typically last-value-wins on most controllers — the earlier value is silently dropped, which usually hides a programming mistake. |
| `CG_DUPLICATE_O_HEADER` | Use a unique O-number per program; rename duplicate O-header | Two O-number headers with the same value make subprogram and call targets ambiguous — the controller picks one (usually the last) silently. |
| `CG_FANUC_INVALID_N_O_FORMAT` | Use an integer N or O value within 1..99999999 | Fanuc sequence (N) and program (O) numbers must be integer values in 1..99999999; fractional, negative, or out-of-range values alarm at the controller. |
| `CG_FANUC_MACRO_IJK_ORDER` | Reorder arguments so I appears before J before K | Fanuc Macro (G65) documentation expects I, J, K arguments in alphabetical order; out-of-order args bind to the wrong macro variables. |
| `CG_FANUC_PROGRAM_ENVELOPE` | Move executable blocks below the O-number header | Most Fanuc controls require the O-number header to be the first executable block; setup or motion blocks before it are dropped or treated as a separate (unnamed) program. |
| `CG_N_AND_O_MIXED` | Move N number to a separate block from the O header | Fanuc manuals state sequence numbers (N) are invalid on O-number blocks — controllers either drop the N silently or alarm. |

### `CG_DUPLICATE_ADDRESSES_*`

- **Canonical fix:** Split duplicate <LETTER> words into two blocks; controller is last-value-wins
- **Rationale:** Duplicated address letters in one block are typically last-value-wins on most controllers — the earlier value is silently dropped, which usually hides a programming mistake.

**Replacement template:**

```
{{FIRST_BLOCK_WITH_LETTER}}
{{SECOND_BLOCK_WITH_LETTER}}
```

### `CG_DUPLICATE_O_HEADER`

- **Canonical fix:** Use a unique O-number per program; rename duplicate O-header
- **Rationale:** Two O-number headers with the same value make subprogram and call targets ambiguous — the controller picks one (usually the last) silently.

**Replacement template:**

```
O{{UNIQUE_PROGRAM_NUMBER}}
```

### `CG_FANUC_INVALID_N_O_FORMAT`

- **Canonical fix:** Use an integer N or O value within 1..99999999
- **Rationale:** Fanuc sequence (N) and program (O) numbers must be integer values in 1..99999999; fractional, negative, or out-of-range values alarm at the controller.

**Replacement template:**

```
{{LETTER}}{{INTEGER_1_TO_99999999}}
```

### `CG_FANUC_MACRO_IJK_ORDER`

- **Canonical fix:** Reorder arguments so I appears before J before K
- **Rationale:** Fanuc Macro (G65) documentation expects I, J, K arguments in alphabetical order; out-of-order args bind to the wrong macro variables.

**Replacement template:**

```
G65 P{{PROG}} I{{I}} J{{J}} K{{K}}
```

### `CG_FANUC_PROGRAM_ENVELOPE`

- **Canonical fix:** Move executable blocks below the O-number header
- **Rationale:** Most Fanuc controls require the O-number header to be the first executable block; setup or motion blocks before it are dropped or treated as a separate (unnamed) program.

**Replacement template:**

```
O{{PROGRAM_NUMBER}}
{{EXECUTABLE_BLOCKS}}
```

### `CG_N_AND_O_MIXED`

- **Canonical fix:** Move N number to a separate block from the O header
- **Rationale:** Fanuc manuals state sequence numbers (N) are invalid on O-number blocks — controllers either drop the N silently or alarm.

**Replacement template:**

```
{{N_BLOCK}}
{{O_BLOCK}}
```
